\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਮੁਲਾਕਾਤ} (mulākāt)}{ਮੁਲਾਕਾਤ (mulākāt)}]{\pa{ਮੁਲਾਕਾਤ} (mulākāt) — a meeting with someone}

\label{lesson:PA-C312-mulakat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to snatch, then the Punjabi for damage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਮੁਲਾਕਾਤ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਮੁਲਾਕਾਤ}} — \emph{mulākāt} — \textquotedblleft{}a meeting with someone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਪਿਛਲੇ} \pa{ਹਫ਼ਤੇ} \pa{ਮੇਰੀ} \pa{ਅਮਨ} \pa{ਨਾਲ} \pa{ਮੁਲਾਕਾਤ} \pa{ਹੋਈ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pichhle hafte merī Aman nāl mulākāt hoī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I met Aman last week.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਮੁਲਾਕਾਤ}} (\emph{mulākāt}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{mulāqāt}, \textquotedblleft{}a meeting\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mulākāt}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mulākāt}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pichhle hafte merī Aman nāl mulākāt hoī.} — I met Aman last week.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for to snatch, then the Punjabi for damage, then say \emph{mulākāt} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \pa{ਮੁਲਾਕਾਤ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A meeting with someone\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਸੱਦਣਾ} (saddṇā)}{ਸੱਦਣਾ (saddṇā)}]{\pa{ਸੱਦਣਾ} (saddṇā) — to invite}

\label{lesson:PA-C312-saddna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for damage, then the Punjabi for a meeting with someone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਸੱਦਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਸੱਦਣਾ}} — \emph{saddṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to invite\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਪਿਛਲੇ} \pa{ਹਫ਼ਤੇ} \pa{ਅਸੀਂ} \pa{ਅਮਨ} \pa{ਨੂੰ} \pa{ਰੋਟੀ} \pa{ਲਈ} \pa{ਸੱਦਿਆ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pichhle hafte asīṁ Aman nū̃ roṭī laī saddiā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last week we invited Aman for a meal.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਆਪਣੇ} \pa{ਦੋਸਤ} \pa{ਨੂੰ} \pa{ਘਰ} \pa{ਸੱਦਿਆ}, \emph{maiṁ āpṇe dost nū̃ ghar saddiā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਸੱਦਣਾ}} (\emph{saddṇā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{śabdayati}, \textquotedblleft{}calls\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{saddṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}called\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 12300).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saddṇā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pichhle hafte asīṁ Aman nū̃ roṭī laī saddiā.} — Last week we invited Aman for a meal.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for damage, then the Punjabi for a meeting with someone, then say \emph{saddṇā} again
  \item \emph{Write it:} copy \textbf{\pa{ਸੱਦਣਾ}} once, checking the whole word
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਖੜਕਾਉਣਾ} (khaṛkāuṇā)}{ਖੜਕਾਉਣਾ (khaṛkāuṇā)}]{\pa{ਖੜਕਾਉਣਾ} (khaṛkāuṇā) — to knock on a door}

\label{lesson:PA-C312-kharkauna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for a meeting with someone, then the Punjabi for to invite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਖੜਕਾਉਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਖੜਕਾਉਣਾ}} — \emph{khaṛkāuṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to knock on a door\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਸ਼ਾਮ} \pa{ਨੂੰ} \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਅਮਨ} \pa{ਦਾ} \pa{ਦਰਵਾਜ਼ਾ} \pa{ਖੜਕਾਇਆ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shām nū̃ maiṁ Aman dā darvāzā khaṛkāiā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the evening I knocked on Aman's door.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਖਿੜਕੀ} \pa{ਖੜਕਾਈ}, \emph{maiṁ khiṛkī khaṛkāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਖੜਕਾਉਣਾ}} (\emph{khaṛkāuṇā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{khaṭakhaṭāyate}, \textquotedblleft{}crackles\textquotedblright{}, an imitative word; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{khaṛkāuṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}to make rattle, thump\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 3771).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khaṛkāuṇā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shām nū̃ maiṁ Aman dā darvāzā khaṛkāiā.} — In the evening I knocked on Aman's door.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for a meeting with someone, then the Punjabi for to invite, then say \emph{khaṛkāuṇā} again
  \item \emph{Write it:} copy \textbf{\pa{ਖੜਕਾਉਣਾ}} once, checking the whole word
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਮੇਜ਼ਬਾਨ} (mezbān)}{ਮੇਜ਼ਬਾਨ (mezbān)}]{\pa{ਮੇਜ਼ਬਾਨ} (mezbān) — a host}

\label{lesson:PA-C312-mezban}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to invite, then the Punjabi for to knock on a door.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਮੇਜ਼ਬਾਨ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਮੇਜ਼ਬਾਨ}} — \emph{mezbān} — \textquotedblleft{}a host\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਉਸ} \pa{ਸ਼ਾਮ} \pa{ਸਾਡਾ} \pa{ਮੇਜ਼ਬਾਨ} \pa{ਬਹੁਤ} \pa{ਖ਼ੁਸ਼} \pa{ਸੀ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us shām sāḍā mezbān bahut khush sī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That evening our host was very happy.
\end{quote}

A masculine or feminine noun, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਮੇਜ਼ਬਾਨ}} (\emph{mezbān}) is a loan, usually traced to Persian \emph{mezbān}, \textquotedblleft{}a host\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਤੋਹਫ਼ਾ} (tohfā)}{ਤੋਹਫ਼ਾ (tohfā)}]{\pa{ਤੋਹਫ਼ਾ} (tohfā) — a gift}

\label{lesson:PA-C312-tohfa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to knock on a door, then the Punjabi for a host.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਤੋਹਫ਼ਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਤੋਹਫ਼ਾ}} — \emph{tohfā} — \textquotedblleft{}a gift\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਮਹਿਮਾਨ} \pa{ਬੱਚਿਆਂ} \pa{ਲਈ} \pa{ਤੋਹਫ਼ੇ} \pa{ਲਿਆਏ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mahimān bachchiāṁ laī tohfe liāe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The guests brought gifts for the children.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਤੋਹਫ਼ਾ}} (\emph{tohfā}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{tuḥfa}, \textquotedblleft{}a gift, a rarity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
